description: Data or comparison table. Wraps in a horizontal-scroll container whenever the table is wider than the band — at ANY viewport, not only on mobile: .table-wrap declares overflow-x: auto with no media query, and the table itself is width: max-content; min-width: 100%. Headers become <th scope='col'> elements. REBUILT ON THE UNIVERSAL DESIGN CONTRACT (v2): it declares no style slots. Every designable value — colour, type, spacing, border, shadow, size, motion — is set through the `udc` map on the band, per role. See docs/v2/BUILD-SPEC-sprint0.md §3.

id.description: Optional HTML id attribute for anchor linking (e.g. navigation anchors). Also becomes the component's stable id.

rows.description: Array of rows. Each row is an array of cell values. Rich HTML (sanitized via wp_kses_post): block markup, lists and links are allowed in a cell, the same contract as section.body.

caption.description: Accessible table caption (rendered as <caption>). Recommended for data tables.

_band.description: The band itself — the <section>. THE DEFAULTS ARE WHAT v1'S BAND RENDERED, measured in Chromium at 375/768/1280 rather than read off the stylesheet: the shared band rhythm and NOTHING ELSE. There is no `background.fill` default because v1's `.table-section` measured `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` — transparent — and there is no border default because it measured 0px/none on all four edges, so the issue-332 border-immunity baseline in `pp-v1` has nothing of table's to erase. That is the difference from faq, whose unthemed band painted `@color-surface`, and from cta, whose band draws a 1px rule top and bottom. table is ALSO the only component in the whole migration that retires NO prop: it never declared `theme` and its `variant_classes` were already empty, so its entire change is slots to roles. `background.position` IS declared, and it is not dead: a band background image is `background.image` (an attachment id) with `background.overlay` for the scrim — a capability table never had on v1 — and this default is CONSISTENCY with section, cta and faq rather than the thing that prevents a top-left crop — the engine's own image companions (PP_UDC_BACKGROUND_IMAGE_COMPANIONS) already append `background-position: center` into the AUTHORED block whenever an image is present, and that block is unlayered, so this pp-zero default is unreachable in exactly the scenario it appears to guard. It is declared so every v2 band's `_band` reads the same; it is otherwise inert. (section's identical default IS a faithful port of a real v1 slot; table and embed had none, so this is the only reason on record for theirs.) SETTING `typography.color` HERE RE-INKS THE HEADING AND NOTHING ELSE YOU PROBABLY MEAN. The `heading` role follows this write through `currentColor`. Nothing else does, and the reason is that THE TABLE PAINTS ITS OWN LIGHT SURFACE, TWO LAYERS DEEP: `table` fills `@color-bg` and `head` fills `@color-surface`, both of which stay light when you darken this band, exactly as faq's items stay light on a dark faq band. So the ink roles split into two groups that need opposite treatment. ON THE TABLE'S OWN LIGHT SURFACE, and CORRECT as they are: `header` (on the head fill) and `cell` (on the table fill) pin `@color-text`, and a dark band must NOT re-ink them — doing so puts light text on a light table. ON THIS BAND'S FILL, and STRANDED by a dark write: `caption` and `empty`, both pinned `@color-muted`. `caption` is the one that is easy to miss and the reason is structural rather than visual: a <caption> box renders OUTSIDE the table's background box (CSS 2.1 §17.4), so `table`'s `@color-bg` never paints behind it — it sits on this band's fill like a bare paragraph. Measured: `@color-muted` (#5e6677) on an authored `@color-bg-inverted` band is about 3.1:1, under the 4.5:1 AA floor for the caption's 14px. A DARK TABLE BAND THEREFORE COSTS THREE WRITES: this role's fill, `caption` ink and `empty` ink. If you also darken `table`'s fill you owe `cell` ink; if you darken `head`'s you owe `header` ink — two separate surfaces and two separate debts, not one pair. Either way you also owe `cell-link`, because a link's colour is a direct declaration that neither `cell` nor the band can reach. `caption` is NOT part of that group: it was never on those surfaces. THE FILL AND THE INK ARE TWO WRITES, AND SETTING ONLY THE FIRST IS THE COMMON MISTAKE: `currentColor` on the `heading` role follows this band's `typography.color`, NOT its `background.fill`. A band given a dark fill and no ink keeps the inherited `@color-text` and renders its heading at about 1.04:1 against the `#101418` fill the rendered e2e case injects (1.006:1 against `@color-bg-inverted` — the two figures are the same mechanism on two different darks, and both are stated so neither reads as a contradiction of the other). Measured, and pinned as a rendered e2e case so the half-done band is a fact rather than a warning. Write `background.fill` and `typography.color` together, always.

heading.description: The band heading (an <h2>). ITS `typography.color` IS `currentColor`, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM THE LITERAL v1 DECLARATION rather than a transcription of it. v1's rule was `color: var(--table-heading-color, var(--color-text))` — a pinned literal — so the literally faithful port would be `@color-text`. The reason it is not: v1 COULD NOT MAKE A DARK TABLE BAND AT ALL. table declared no `theme` prop and `variant_classes: []`, so `@color-text` is the only thing this heading ever rendered, and it is identical to `currentColor` on every band v1 could express. They diverge only where v1 was inexpressible — an authored `_band.background.fill`, which v2 makes trivial — and carrying the literal would pin the heading against the one band shape v2 newly makes easy. That is the defect #1026 shipped on cta and corrected. `currentColor` in the `color` property is defined to mean `inherit`, so an authored `_band` -> `typography.color` reaches this heading and an authored value on THIS role still wins. ITS WEIGHT, LEADING, TRACKING, FAMILY AND `text-wrap` ARE NOT RESTATED, and that is the opposite call from faq's heading for a measured reason rather than an inconsistency: faq's weight and leading came from `main > .faq .faq__heading` rules that existed ONLY inside media queries, so dropping them would have restyled every tier. table has no such rules — measured 650 / 1.2 ratio / -0.03em / system-ui / balance at all three tiers, every one of them from base.css's shared `h1`-`h6` rule — and restating a global value here would move it to the unlayered tier and beat that rule in every state. NO `text-align` EITHER: measured `start` with `margin-left: 0px` at every tier, which is the initial value and not a declaration. Do not add auto margins here reaching for stats' centred heading; this heading is left-pinned by design and always was.

wrap.description: The scroll container around the table — the framed box a reader actually sees the edge of. Its border and radius are the frame; the SCROLLING is structural and stays in the stylesheet, because `overflow-x: auto`, `overscroll-behavior-x: contain`, `-webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch`, `width` and `max-width` are the affordance rather than a design value, and the whole point of this component is that the scroll is VIEWPORT-INDEPENDENT (no media query, guarded by DocsCoverageTest). TWO of those five had no classification in the structural-CSS lint before this rebuild — `overscroll-behavior-x` and `-webkit-overflow-scrolling` — and both were claimed into STRUCTURAL at #1066 with a stated reason, the way `cursor`, `transition` and `transform` were at #994. `overflow-x`, `width` and `max-width` were already structural and are named here only because they are part of the same affordance. (An earlier draft of this sentence said four were unclassified while listing five, which the fail-closed arm this rebuild pins makes impossible: an unclassified property fails CI the moment the component joins the boundary rule.) Declares no `background` default: measured transparent, so the table's own fill is what shows through the frame.

table.description: The <table> itself. ITS FILL IS `@color-bg` AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING FOR THE INK INSIDE IT, the same way faq's item fill is: the table stays light on a dark band, which is why `cell` pins its colour instead of following the band. THE CONSEQUENCE IS YOURS TO CARRY: if you darken this fill, set `cell` -> `typography.color` in the same write, and `header` too if you darkened `head`. `border-collapse: collapse` stays STRUCTURAL — it selects the border BOX MODEL rather than any border value, the `box-sizing` tier — but it is NOT inert, and the `row` role's description says what it does to the edges. `width: max-content` and `min-width: 100%` are structural too: they are what make the wrapper scroll instead of the table squashing. Its `typography.size` is a flat `0.9375rem`, measured identical at all three tiers, and `cell` deliberately declares no size of its own so it inherits this one.

caption.description: The accessible <caption>, rendered below the table. IT IS NOT ON THE TABLE'S SURFACE, and that is the fact worth carrying away: a caption box renders OUTSIDE the table's background box (CSS 2.1 §17.4), so `table` -> `background.fill` never paints behind it — it sits on the BAND fill, like a bare paragraph in the container. That makes it a sibling of `empty` rather than of `cell`, and it is the role a dark-band write strands. Measured: its `@color-muted` (#5e6677) on an authored `@color-bg-inverted` band is about 3.1:1, under the 4.5:1 AA floor for 14px body text. ITS `typography.align` IS A REAL DECLARATION, not a reset that could be dropped: the HTML rendering spec gives `caption` a centred default, and this left alignment is table's own rule defeating it. Dropping it would centre every caption on every site. `caption-side: bottom` stays STRUCTURAL — it decides WHERE the box goes, the `position`/`order` tier, and no group emits it.

head.description: The <thead> band across the top of the table. Its fill is `@color-surface`, a light tint ON TOP of the table's own light `@color-bg` — and like the table's fill it stays light when you darken the band, which is why `header` pins its ink. IT COMPETES WITH `header` FOR ONE VISUAL LINE, and the ranking is not the cascade: under `border-collapse: collapse` a shared edge is resolved by CSS 2.1 §17.6.2, whose last tiebreak is the ELEMENT the border was declared on — cell beats row beats rowgroup. This role is the ROWGROUP, so a border declared here loses a tie to the same border declared on `header`, whatever the source order or specificity. Declare the rule on `header` unless you specifically want the weaker claim.

header.description: One column header — a <th scope="col">. TWO OF ITS DEFAULTS DEFEAT BROWSER DEFAULTS AND MUST NOT BE READ AS RESETS TO TIDY AWAY: the HTML rendering spec gives `th` a CENTRED, BOLD presentation, and v1 declared `text-align: left` and `font-weight: 700` as table's own rules to override the first and to pin the second. Dropping the alignment centres every header on every site; dropping the weight would leave the browser's `bold` in charge, which happens to compute to 700 today and is not a guarantee this theme should outsource. Note that the global-value rule does NOT cover this case — that rule is about the THEME's own layered rules changing tier when they become role defaults, and a browser default lives in the UA origin, which loses to any author declaration whatever layer it sits in. Its `color` PINS `@color-text` because this cell sits on `head`'s light `@color-surface` fill, which stays light on a dark band. ITS BOTTOM RULE NOW SHARES AN EDGE WITH `row`'s TOP RULE, and that is new in v2: 2px beats `row`'s 1px today, so nothing moves — but if you set this to `1px` you create a WIDTH TIE, which §17.6.2 breaks by element rank, so this <th> wins and an authored `row` -> `border.color-top` silently paints nothing at that one edge. On v1 the two edges were independent. `white-space: nowrap` stays structural.

row.description: One body row — a <tr>. ITS SEPARATOR IS ON THE TOP EDGE, WHERE v1'S WAS ON THE BOTTOM, and that move is the whole of how this rebuild keeps a capability the role grammar cannot spell. v1 drew `border-bottom` on every row and then suppressed it with `.table__row:last-child { border-bottom: none }`. THE REASON THAT PAIR CANNOT SURVIVE IS THE LAYER MODEL, not the selector charset: the base separator becomes an in-band ELEMENT role default, which emits UNLAYERED, while a `:last-child` suppression would stay in `pp-v1` — and unlayered beats every layer at any specificity, so the suppression would simply stop working. (The charset cannot spell `:last-child` either, but that is beside the point; a structural pseudo-class is also not one of the three states `pp_udc_states()` defines.) Moving the separator to the TOP edge reproduces v1 exactly, because `border-collapse: collapse` MERGES adjacent edges and the wider one wins: row 1's new 1px top edge merges into `header`'s 2px bottom rule and disappears into it, and the last row simply has no bottom edge. Verified before it shipped — 1, 2 and 3 rows at 375/768/1280, row boxes, gaps and painted screenshots all byte-identical to v1. THE `style` HALF IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT DECORATION: `border-style`'s initial value is `none`, which is the LOWEST priority in the collapse model, so a width and a colour with no `style-top` paint NOTHING. Set them together or not at all. TWO COLLAPSE BEHAVIOURS HAVE NO v1 EQUIVALENT AND ARE WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU MEET THEM: `border.style-top: "hidden"` ERASES `header`'s 2px rule entirely, because `hidden` beats every width in §17.6.2; and `border.width-top: "3px"` overrides it, because wider wins. `:hover` IS A REAL MEASURED STATE, not an invention — v1 tinted a hovered row to `@color-surface` and this carries it. The `transition` property LIST stays structural (ruling A3 gives motion exactly two params, and a property list is neither); `motion.transition-duration` retunes the 0.15s without widening what is animated. THIS ROLE DECLARES NO `typography`, AND THAT IS A CHECKED OMISSION RATHER THAN A GAP: a colour on a <tr> reaches its cells only by INHERITANCE, and `cell` pins `@color-text` as a direct declaration on the <td> — so the group would be accepted at write, stored, reported applied, and paint nothing. That is the accepted-but-inert class the contract exists to end, so the group is withheld rather than offered. Set `cell` -> `typography.color` instead; it is the element the ink actually lands on.

cell.description: One body cell — a <td>, and the component's rich-text surface: a cell takes block markup, lists and links through wp_kses_post(), the same contract as section.body. ITS COLOUR PINS `@color-text` because it sits on `table`'s light `@color-bg` fill, which stays light when you darken the band — see the `_band` role for the full split. IT DECLARES NO SIZE AND NO LEADING, deliberately, and the two absences have different reasons: the 15px it renders is INHERITED from the `table` role's `typography.size`, so declaring it here would pin a value the parent already owns and silently break `table` -> `typography.size` for every cell; the 1.6 leading comes from base.css's body rule, a global value, and restating it would move it to the unlayered tier. `vertical-align: top`, `white-space: normal` and `overflow-wrap: anywhere` stay STRUCTURAL — the first two are how cells of differing height relate, and the third is the affordance that lets a long unbroken token fit its column. That last one is why table is the only band component whose stressed render does NOT scroll the page sideways at 375px: `break-word` (what base.css gives the page) breaks a word visually but does not reduce intrinsic min-content size, while `anywhere` does. stats and logos lack it and overflow; see #1067.

obligations.why: A colour here lands on the wrapper and reaches an <a> inside it only by inheritance, while the stylesheet gives every anchor its own direct rule. Set the paired link role named above too, and its `:hover`.

cell-link.description: A link an author wrote into a cell's rich text. IT DECLARES NO DEFAULTS, AND THE EMPTY BLOCK IS THE POINT rather than an oversight — the same shape section's `body-link` and cta's `body-link` already ship. Measured, a link in a cell renders `@color-accent` underlined, byte-identical to what base.css gives every anchor on the page, and a role block is emitted UNLAYERED: restating those values as a DEFAULT would outrank the shared premium button rules for an author-written `<a class="btn">` in a cell, which is the #545 defect reintroduced through a role selector. So the rule is that rule 2 forbids a DEFAULT, not a ROLE. With no default this role emits nothing at rest — zero cascade movement — while still giving an author an ADDRESS, which is what a dark surface needs: a container role's `typography.color` reaches a link only by INHERITANCE, and base.css's `a` rule is a direct declaration on the element, so an inherited value can never beat it (measured on faq, #1069). An authored colour HERE does win, because it is aimed at the element itself. If you darken `table` -> `background.fill`, set this as well as `cell` — `cell` alone leaves every link at `@color-accent` on your dark fill. IT CARRIES STATES, AND v1'S AUTOMATIC REMAP CARRIED TWO. The retired rule was a PAIR — the resting colour and its `:hover` — and what a resting-ONLY write does here is not what it sounds like, so it is stated measured rather than reasoned: the authored value emits UNLAYERED, and unlayered beats every layer, so it wins on hover too. The link then holds one colour in both states and STOPS RESPONDING TO HOVER AT ALL. A lost affordance, not a contrast failure — the contrast failure is the different case where NOTHING is written here and the link sits at `@color-accent`, 3.23:1 on `@color-bg-inverted`. Write `typography.color` and `typography.:hover.color` in the same map; a role's states move with its resting value. AND THE AUTHORED VALUE REACHES A COMPOSED BUTTON, WHICH THE DEFAULT WAS FORBIDDEN FOR — stated because a route that discloses half a consequence is a route that lies. An authored colour here emits `[data-pp-band="<id>"] <selector>` UNLAYERED, and that matches an author-written `<a class="btn">` in this surface just as it matches a prose link, in every state. v1 did NOT do this: the retired class rule weighed (0,1,1) INSIDE `pp-v1` and lost to `main .btn:not(...)` at (0,4,1), so the automatic remap left buttons alone. Measured, the dark-band write this role is for puts `@color-accent-on-inverted` on the premium gradient's `@color-accent` at 2.58:1, where the button's own `@color-bg` label is 5.37:1. The selector CANNOT be narrowed to `a:not(.btn)` today — the role-selector charset admits neither `:` nor `(` — so the remedy is to avoid a composed button in a surface whose links you are recolouring, or to accept the button taking the same ink. Filed as a narrowing question rather than worked around here.

empty.description: The "No data." line a band with no headers or no rows renders. ITS COLOUR IS A ROLE DEFAULT AND THE MARKUP LOST A UTILITY CLASS TO MAKE THAT TRUE. v1 rendered this grey by putting `text-muted` on the element, which hardcodes `--color-muted` from utilities.css in `@layer pp-v1`; footer met the identical case at #994 and faq at #1046, and both ruled it the same way — the template drops the class so the role governs. WHICH WRITE THAT CLASS WOULD HAVE BEATEN is worth stating exactly, because it is half-true in both directions: a write aimed at THIS role emits unlayered and matches `.table-section__empty` directly, so it beats the layered utility and the class never blocked it; a `_band` write reaches this line only by INHERITANCE, and an inherited value is used only when no declaration matches the element, so layer order never enters and `.text-muted` wins. The `_band` write is the one the class stranded, which is the dark-band case. LIKE `caption`, THIS LINE SITS ON THE BAND FILL, so a dark band needs a write here — and unlike `cell` it is never inside the table's own light surface. Its padding is table's own rule (`@space-md` top and bottom, measured 16px), not a global: base.css zeroes every element's padding, so dropping it would close the line up against the heading above it.
